Reading GetUser in user_service.

Checking SQLite driver initialization and store driver creation in the database layer.

Tracing the request flow for another user's profile image. Browser requests `/file/users/{username}/avatar` via an `` tag. `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` maps this to `serveUserAvatar`. That function calls `getUserByUsername`, then `Store.GetUser`, then `driver.ListUsers` against SQLite. The avatar URL is read from the `avatar_url` column. `parseDataURI` decodes the base64 data URI. Finally `c.Blob` returns the image bytes. The avatar is stored as a base64 data URI inside the `user.avatar_url` column. It is not a separate disk file. The `auth.AuthenticateToUser` hop applies to private instances. `getCurrentUser` is used within `serveUserAvatar`. The concrete file paths are now mapped. - `RegisterRoutes` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` - `serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` - `getCurrentUser` → `AuthenticateToUser` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` → `server/auth/authenticator.go` - `getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` - `Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go` - `Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go` - `driver.ListUsers` — `store/driver.go` - SQLite `ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (or postgres/mysql) The browser-side path is now clear. The `UserAvatar` component renders the image via `img src={avatarUrl}` in `web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx`. The `avatarUrl` originates from the API response as `/file/users/{username}/avatar`, generated by `convertUserFromStore` in `user_service_converters.go`. The browser fetches the image as a separate GET request, independent of the API call. The Echo router is wired into `http.Server` in `server.go`. The data driver is initialized in `store/db/db.go` and opened in `store/db/sqlite.go`.

The request enters through `server/server.go`, where `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` maps the route to `serveUserAvatar`. Authentication runs through `getCurrentUser` and `authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` and `server/auth/authenticator.go`. The handler then calls `getUserByUsername` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`, which delegates to `Store.GetUser` in `store/user.go`. That method resolves the user via `Store.ListUsers` on the driver interface in `store/driver.go`, ultimately executing a SQL `SELECT avatar_url` against the default SQLite driver in `store/db/sqlite/user.go`. Finally, `parseDataURI` decodes the returned data URI in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. The final hop is `c.Blob` returning image bytes in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. The avatar lives as a base64-encoded data URI inside the `avatar_url` column of the `user` table, not as a separate file. The trace will list every hop with its symbol and path. The trace should focus on the GET /file/users/.../avatar path itself. The browser may first call an API endpoint to retrieve user metadata including avatarUrl. Then it issues a second request to the avatar endpoint. The serving handler and each hop to the data layer are the key targets. Username-based lookups bypass the user cache entirely. `Store.GetUser` calls `ListUsers` directly without checking `userCache`, so the request reaches the driver immediately. The SQLite database file is located at `memos_prod.db` in the data directory, configured by `profile.DSN` in `internal/profile/profile.go`. Other drivers such as MySQL and PostgreSQL implement equivalent `ListUsers` methods in `store/db/mysql/user.go` and `store/db/postgres/user.go`. The avatar data URI is stored directly in the `avatar_url` TEXT column, with no separate file on disk.

value.text:
Verifying that `convertUserFromStore` generates the browser's avatar URL path.

The avatar is stored as a base64 data URI in the `avatar_url` column of the `user` table. After `parseDataURI`, the bytes are served from memory. The trace begins at `RegisterRoutes` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`.

`serveUserAvatar` and `getCurrentUser` are in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. `AuthenticateToUser` is in `server/auth/authenticator.go`. `getUserByUsername` is in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. `GetUser` is in `store/user.go`. `ListUsers` is in `store/user.go` and `store/db/sqlite/user.go`. `QueryContext` is in `store/db/sqlite/user.go`. `parseDataURI` is in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. The default database driver is SQLite.

The per-request trace ends at `QueryContext` in `store/db/sqlite/user.go`, where `rows.Scan` reads the avatar data from the `user.avatar_url` column. `sql.Open` via `NewDB` is a startup connection step, not a per-request hop.

`FileServerService` wiring in `server.go` is included as the hop connecting the router to the handler.

h07. The browser loads another user's avatar after the API returns a URL like `/file/users/{username}/avatar` (rewritten from the stored data URI in `convertUserFromStore` at `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go`). The `` in `UserAvatar` then issues `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar`. That request reaches stored data as follows (avatar bytes live in the `user.avatar_url` DB column as a base64 data URI, not as a separate file): RegisterRoutes — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go getCurrentUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go AuthenticateToUser — server/auth/authenticator.go getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go GetUser — store/user.go ListUsers — store/user.go ListUsers — store/db/sqlite/user.go QueryContext (SELECT avatar_url FROM user) — store/db/sqlite/user.go parseDataURI — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go Notes: - Route registration happens in `server/server.go` via `fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)`. - On private instances (`Profile.AllowAnonymous()` is false), `getCurrentUser`/`AuthenticateToUser` must succeed before the lookup proceeds (`internal/profile/profile.go`). - The DB driver is selected at startup in `store/db/db.go` (`sqlite` by default in `cmd/memos/main.go`; `mysql` and `postgres` use equivalent `ListUsers` in `store/db/mysql/user.go` and `store/db/postgres/user.go`). - After `avatar_url` is read, `parseDataURI` decodes the data URI into raw image bytes returned by `c.Blob` in `serveUserAvatar`.
